topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and outlines the scope and focus of the lecture on inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the foundational concepts of how the innate immune system detects infections and tissue injury through conserved molecular patterns and cellular receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor pathways and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific receptor families, their intracellular signaling mechanisms, and the inflammasome complex responsible for processing inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Effector cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell trafficking to sites of infection and draining lymph nodes, along with the dangers of severe systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the active and passive mechanisms that conclude inflammatory responses, the processes of tissue healing, and the physiological role of chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and announces the topic of the following lecture.
